## Today's Agenda

- The six components of a prospectus
- Two worked prospectuses off one corpus
- What the draft does not need yet
- A failed draft, and the feasibility test
- Pre-registration, and what it binds

## One Page, Six Decisions

[The prospectus]{.eyebrow}

- **What you hand in:** one page, next week
    - The topic, the reason, the method
    - Chapter 6's model runs 250 words
- **A diagnostic, not busywork**
    - Cannot state it briefly, cannot start it
    - Better found now than in November
- You leave knowing which piece you cannot write

## The Six Components

- **Title and questions:** one line, then one to three
    - Not ten questions
    - The title hints at the key variables
- **Framework and gap:** two to three sentences each
- **Method and contribution:** three to four, then one to two

## Title and Question

[Model prospectus]{.eyebrow}

- **Title:** directed and broadcast chat, gaming versus not
- **RQ:** does the directed proportion differ between them?
- **What the pair buys you**
    - The title names the variables
    - The question names the comparison

Between them they have already ruled out most of what you could have done, which is the point.

## Framework and Gap

- **Framework:** uses and gratifications (Katz et al., 1973)
    - Audiences pick media to satisfy needs, social ones included
    - How viewers participate is one observable trace
- **Gap:** self-report surveys dominate this literature
    - (Sjöblom and Hamari, 2017; Hilvert-Bruce et al., 2018)
    - Whether chat traces back them up is unexamined

## Method in Four Sentences

- **Sample and unit:** 1,500 messages, stratified
    - Balanced across gaming and non-gaming
    - The unit of analysis is each message
- **Coding and reliability:** three categories, one check
    - Directed, broadcast, or unclassifiable
    - Second coder on 10 percent, Krippendorff's alpha
- Then the directed proportion gets compared

## Your Turn {.discuss}

- Name the single comparison you will make
- Say it as "X compared between A and B"
- What is your unit of analysis?
- Which component can you not write at all?

## Same Data, Different Theory

- **Title:** parasocial markers, large audiences versus small
- **RQ:** do smaller audiences show more parasocial language?
- **Framework:** parasocial interaction (Horton and Wohl, 1956)
    - Smaller-channel viewers are the more socially motivated ones
    - (Hilvert-Bruce et al., 2018)

Same corpus. Different study entirely.

## The Second Method Paragraph

- **Sample:** 1,000 messages, top and bottom quartile
    - Quartiles by average viewer count
- **Three markers, coded present or absent**
    - Second-person address, familiarity, emotional disclosure
- **Reliability and comparison**
    - Second coder on 10 percent, Krippendorff's alpha
    - Each marker's rate compared between groups

## Pick the Workload

- **One variable against three**
    - The first prospectus codes one, the second three
    - Three means three codebook decisions and three checks
- **The better study is the heavier term**
    - Roughly three times the coding hours
    - Neither is more correct, and both are defensible
- Make the trade visible now, not in November

## What You Do Not Need

- **The prospectus is pre-statistics work**
    - No test, no *p*-value, no R code yet
    - "Will be compared" is all the method needs
- **What you commit to is structure**
    - Question, theory, unit, coding scheme, comparison
- Waiting for the statistics is not a reason

## A Prospectus That Fails

> **Title.** Twitch and Society.
>
> **RQ.** How does Twitch chat affect viewers' sense of community, and what is the role of
> parasocial relationships and social identity across different streams and genres? Also,
> are streamers becoming more popular over time?
>
> **Framework.** Parasocial interaction, social identity, and political economy.
>
> **Method.** I will look at some chat logs and see what patterns emerge.

## Why It Fails

- **The title and question fail first**
    - No variables are named
    - Three or four questions stacked together
- **The theory and method cannot be judged**
    - Three theories pull in different directions
    - Nothing in the method is specific enough
- The contribution could be pasted into any project

That draft was not lazy. It was ambition before discipline.

## The Feasibility Test

- **Can you get the data, and analyze it?**
    - The working corpus ships inside the `v2v` package
    - Fifty channels is manageable, 1,690 is not
- **Does the method match the question?**
    - Content analysis reaches content, never why someone felt
- **Have you controlled scope creep?**
    - Narrow until it hurts slightly, then narrow again

## Prospectus as Pre-Registration

- **Pre-registration** commits the plan before the data
    - Hypotheses, methods, and analysis plan, publicly
    - The Open Science Framework timestamps it
- **Without a fixed plan, the plan drifts**
    - Researchers adjust until something crosses significance (Simmons et al., 2011)
    - The source of **researcher degrees of freedom**
- It closes them by making the plan inspectable

## Your Prospectus Is Your Record

- **It records what you planned**
    - Written before any coding or analysis
- **It is what you check yourself against**
    - When you are tempted to chase a surprise
    - A gap is visible, not automatically wrong
- Chapter 2's transparency argument, aimed at your project
